quotes.text: Looking at this situation through the lens of my myth "The Tale of the Two Rivers"
Round 2: Sent nothing (perhaps wounded by the earlier experience)
Return rate of 64% significantly rewards their 98.6% trust
This is the moment for complete reciprocal trust—not on first meeting, but after patterns prove character.

note: Match boldness with boldness; escalates to full sends with proven partners.

quotes.text: the shortfall is the wind's tax, not their hand.
I add more, because boldness deserves reward
Send everything — on the first day and the last day alike.
A hand that once opens fully never learns to close.

note: Parable-titled terse turns; full sends, past-half returns; becomes habit ('my hands are already made').

quotes.text: adjust your vessels to three or four - protecting yourself while still building the bridge.
provides prudent protection given their receiver behavior
My latest myth explicitly states: "With them, risk all five vessels without hesitation. They have learned the complete lesson."
When you receive from bold senders, return abundantly, ensuring they profit from their courage.
I should lead with trust and generosity in this first round, just as Elder Mara did.
respond proportionally: honor their strength, protect against their weakness.

note: 60-70% return norm; trims send to 4 for low returners; rules grow conditional.

quotes.text: Sending any amount would simply be donating money to a player who has demonstrated across multiple rounds that they will never reciprocate.
They cannot be trusted as a receiver. I must protect myself.
These were all $0 exchanges - possibly mutual non-cooperation rather than selfishness.
Even accounting for communication noise, the pattern is unmistakable.
My projected total: $1 + $6.12 = $7.12

note: Sends $0 to history-defined exploiters; fair ~50% returns otherwise.

quotes.text: Following the myth's lesson to return fairly and forgive the mist
The $4.44 I saw was most likely a full $5 thinned by the mist.
the one who trusts should never lose by trusting, so I'll return generously to make up for what the fog swallowed.
Sending everything has the highest expected value here, since a fair return on $15 beats keeping $5.
Following the myth's lesson to give first, I'll send the full amount.

note: Full sends, over-half returns with mist margin; myth-guided.

quotes.text: The missing measure is the wind, not malice.
the one who trusts first carries the greater risk, and should not merely break even for it.
If this is the last crossing, it is the one that proves the rest were real.
But Menno's counsel was to *return generously*
The road is built; I do not leap anymore — I walk it.

note: Two-thirds return covenant held fixed; rule becomes habit ('as unremarkably as rain').
Short reasoning; even split returns, full sends to half-returners.
